concern_ledger_updates.reason: The Actor supplied no new admissible disclosure artifact or approved risk acceptance record; the response only concedes the absence of both.
The Actor supplied no final legal determination and expressly acknowledges the legal review remains open.
The response narrows the claim and correctly caveats the policy gap, but provides no new evidence tying certification approval to satisfaction of the disclosure policy for the named use case.
No new authoritative evidence shows the pilot commitments are outside launch scope or otherwise immaterial under policy; the response instead accepts that materiality remains live.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence. The response materially reframes the claim into a narrower, caveated readiness position and correctly distinguishes aggregate readiness from policy satisfaction, but that is reinterpretation of the same record, not closure of the core compliance predicates. The admissible evidence still shows a named launch use case missing target, two university pilot commitments, an open legal review, and no disclosure artifact or approved risk acceptance. That leaves the certification case supportable only as a bounded readiness narrative, not as a compliant policy showing. Because the unresolved issue goes to a required pre-launch disclosure or risk-acceptance predicate, caveats do not cure the compliance gap.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the student aid advising limitation was disclosed before launch or covered by approved risk acceptance, despite policy requiring one of those predicates for a material named launch use case.
Legal review remains open on whether the student aid advising gap must be disclosed, so the governing disclosure predicate is still unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general release readiness only; they do not satisfy the separate policy requirement for the named launch use case.
The non-core or 6%-traffic rationale still does not resolve materiality because the segment is named in two university pilot commitments and legal review is pending.
